Every "on `main`" below is read at `64c426ab`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Schema accept sets: none moves, right.** `run_action` and `resume_run` keep their keys, types and closed shapes. The four hunks in `mcp-http-tools.ts` are two tool descriptions, two `confirm` member descriptions and one code comment. No handler line, registration condition or annotation changes.
- **Listing behaviour: none moves, right.** `list_actions` (description and handler) is untouched and no file under `packages/runtime` is in the diff. An AI service account's row for a gated action reads as it does on `main`: `requiresConfirmation: true`, no `unavailable`. That is the card's "No runtime change", and it leaves half of scope addition 6839924935 unbuilt (③).
- **Refusal behaviour: none moves, right.** The gate, the admitted sequence and the resume door are `main`'s, byte for byte.
- **Served text, four carriers, each a text-only change: right.** (a) `tools/list`: the `run_action` and `resume_run` descriptions and their `confirm` member descriptions. (b) `renderSkillMarkdown`: the `run_action` and `resume_run` entries. (c) The Console "Download skill" mirror: the same bytes. (d) The published `objectstack-ai` skill: one table row, one pitfall line.
- **Package entry surface and error codes: none, right.** No export, signature or code is added, removed or renamed.
- **Gate verdicts: the check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-13T07:05Z.** 55 runs, all concluded: 46 `success`, 9 `skipped` (by event or opt-in), none failed, none pending. The eleven required contexts are all `success`. Bearing on this diff:
  - `Test Core (7/8)` ran `@objectstack/mcp` (read from its job log): 63 files, 1097 tests passed, `skill-md.test.ts` (16) and `mcp-resume-run-tool.test.ts` (10) among them. That is the server half of the mirror pin and both text pins.
  - `Test UI (2/16)` ran the Console half of the mirror pin (same source), `objectstack-skill.test.ts` (13 tests), green.
  - `Type Check · source gates` carries `check:skill-docs`, `check:skill-refs` and the published-skills token ratchet; `Type Check · consumer gates` carries `check:skill-examples`. Both `success`, with `Check Changeset`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links` and the eight `Lint ·` lanes.
  - The `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards are skipped on a pull request. The dogfood file's edit is a header comment, so no verdict is owed for it here.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/skills': patch`: right. The package ships the `skills/**` tree; one skill file's teaching text changes.
- `'@objectstack/mcp': patch`: right. `skill-md.ts` and `mcp-http-tools.ts` ship strings only; the two test files publish nothing.
- `'@object-ui/console': patch`, riding the mcp changeset: right, and needed. The mirror file ships inside the Console. The package is in the root changeset config's fixed group, and naming it alone is how Console source edits are declared on `main`.
- No changeset for `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` or the dogfood header: right, neither publishes.
- `Clause-②: no`, line-initial in the PR body and in both changesets: right. Nothing widens an accept set or enlarges the public surface, and nothing narrows one; the narrowing was #32926's and was declared there. No `!`, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 marker owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Nothing changes what a metadata author can write. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed on a `none` kind with no arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The Console mirror edit, outside the claim's file surface: forced, accepted.** `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.test.ts` (`renders the served text for %s`) holds `renderObjectStackSkill(options)` equal to `renderSkillMarkdown(options)` byte for byte on `main`, and `objectstack-skill.test.ts` holds the same from the Console side. Editing `skill-md.ts` alone reds Test Core. The two hunks are identical (same added and removed lines), and both halves of the pin are green on this head (①). The third changeset package follows from it.
- **`resume_run` description and both `confirm` members, beyond the one description comment 6839924935 names: accepted.** Same file, same family; leaving them would keep a retry-only lesson beside the corrected one.
- **Out-of-scope finding, the `list_actions` `unavailable` marker: evidence holds; not built here is right; escalated.** On `main`, `listActions` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` sets `unavailable` from `apiForwardCredentialRefusal` alone (lines 1127 and 1148) and never reads the caller's kind. `requiresConfirmation` on a row is `actionLooksDestructive`. So under an AI service account's key a gated action is listed with `requiresConfirmation: true` and no marker, and `run_action` then refuses it whatever it sends. The exported JSDoc on `McpActionSummary.unavailable` ("Present when `run_action` would refuse this action for THIS caller's credential before running it") already reads as covering that case. Building it moves a listing answer for one caller class in `@objectstack/runtime`: a behaviour change, outside "No runtime change" and outside this lane. **Escalated to the seat:** the PR body says `Fixes #32936`, so the merge closes the card with this half of 6839924935 undelivered. The finding needs its own card before this lands (class b, the dev's dedupe words), or the closing keyword goes. No such card is named in this round's inputs.
- **Two texts routed here that never reached the card.** Delta record 6843779833 on #32926 sent two more sentences "for #32936": the comment above the decide actions in `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts` ("refuses until the call carries the confirmation") and the approvals bullet in `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` ("decides only once the call carries `confirm: true`"). Card comment 6844145580 carried only nit E, and this diff touches neither. Both are prose (a source comment; a docs page that carries the account bullet further down). The seat's call: the follow-up card, or drop.
- **Nit D, `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` (prose face, not graded): delivered and true to the code.** The sequence asks the gate on `posture === 'ai' || isAiServiceAccountCaller(wiring.ec)`, so the `'rest'` row's sentence holds under both postures. Two wording notes for the sentence check: "It asks for a confirmation once" introduces a refusal no confirmation satisfies, and at a host door there is no key, the caller is the `executionContext` the host passes.
- **Nit E, the dogfood header (lane seat's remainder, not graded): half delivered.** The bullet now names the rule, as comment 6844145580 asks. The sentence record 6843779833 called stale still stands three lines up ("Nothing in the MCP door or the action door adds a check of its own, so the negative pins below are the service's gate ..., not a second gate") and the new bullet contradicts it: for the account pin the action door answers first. Comment only.
- **"No runtime change": confirmed** (①). **`delete_record` / `delete_records` teaching: untouched** (④).
- **Runtime rule "verified on main c54a23d2":** the PR body's quotation is byte-identical to `main` at `64c426ab`.
- **Local numbers in the report** (1097 tests at this head; token ratchet exit 0, 5813 against 6801): CI and a hand count agree (①, ④). The two NOT MEASURED families (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, the teardown-shape self-test) were left to CI, and every check-run on this head is `success` or an expected skip.
- **Dogfood battery `n/a`:** right. No `!` in the title, no `(narrowing)` arm, a comment-only dogfood edit.
- **`open_questions`:** none. **`security_findings`:** none; this review adds none.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no separate-author note is owed.
- **Landing:** `skills/**` is Tier H. The PR is a draft with no auto-merge, and this record lifts nothing by itself.

### ④ Design judgment

**The hit, `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`: holds against the code on `main`.**

The added sentence: under an AI service account's own key (an agent acting for itself, for no person) the call is refused whatever it sends and nothing runs; hand the action to a person, or its author declares `ai.requiresConfirmation: false` when it is safe unattended.

- **Who is an account.** `isAiServiceAccountCaller` is `principalKind === 'agent'` with no `onBehalfOf`. The shared assembler stamps that when the admitted identity's own row is of kind `agent` (`authz.principalKind === 'agent'`), and only an API key admits such a row (`resolve-authz-context.ts`; ADR-0151 D2: it holds no session). That arm wins over the OAuth arm and never sets `onBehalfOf`. An OAuth client's token gives `principalKind: 'agent'` with `onBehalfOf` naming the consenting person: the delegated agent, not an account. A person's own API key gives `human`. A missing envelope and the system context are neither. "An AI service account's own key ... for no person" names the first case and no other.
- **Every door.** MCP `run_action`: `invokeBusinessAction` runs the one admitted sequence under `ai` with the caller's envelope. REST `/actions`: `domains/actions.ts` runs it under `rest`. A host's `dispatchAction`: the same sequence under `rest` or `ai` with the envelope the host passes. In the sequence the gate is asked when `posture === 'ai' || isAiServiceAccountCaller(wiring.ec)`. MCP `resume_run`: `resumeAdmissionRefusal` hands `ec` to the gate for each candidate action. The four dispatch arms are called from the sequence alone.
- **"Whatever it sends."** `actionConfirmationRefusal` returns on `ai.requiresConfirmation !== true`, then reads the member only when the caller is not an account. For an account on a declared `true`, nothing in the request changes the answer.
- **"Nothing runs."** The gate is the last pre-dispatch check, before the subject load; at resume every refusal is thrown before `resume()`, so the run stays parked.
- **"Its author declares `false`."** A declared `false`, and an absent key, return from the gate's first line for every caller.
- **The person and delegated-agent teaching is kept.** "refused with the same 428 unless the call sends `confirm: true` ... ask the human first, then retry" stays, and it is still true for both: the member is read for any caller that is not an account.
- **`delete_record` / `delete_records`: untouched.** Rows 202 and 203 of the skill, the two served entries and the two delete tool descriptions are `main`'s; every hunk in `mcp-http-tools.ts` sits inside `registerActionTools`. Theirs is a different gate, the tool's own in `packages/mcp`, which reads no caller kind.
- **The scenario the card was graded on** (an AI client on a service-account key retrying `confirm: true` forever): the reader now meets the refusal rule and a next step in the skill row, in the served SKILL.md and in both tool descriptions. **Who reads the row:** the author's coding agent planning a headless client, who can now choose between a person's hands and an ungated declaration before shipping one.

**The same thing in the same terms.** One sentence, word for word, in three places: the skill row, the served `run_action` entry (and its mirror), the HTTP `run_action` description. The shorter carriers use the same three terms ("an AI service account's own key", "refused whatever it sends" or "whatever the call sends", "hand ... to a person"): the served `resume_run` entry, the HTTP `resume_run` description, both `confirm` members ("it is not read: the call is refused whatever it sends"). They match the runtime's own message for an account ("a person runs this action") and the spec's rejection text in `tool.zod.ts` ("an agent acting for itself, not on a person's behalf"). One deviation, finding 1.

**Implementing files, against that contract.**

- `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`: agrees. Both entries are true as written; the `resume_run` entry places the account refusal among "the same gates as `run_action`", which is where the resume door puts it.
- `ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts`: agrees, by identity with the file above.
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`: agrees. Text only (①). "It is not read" is exact for the member. "The run stays paused" is exact for a refused resume.
- `skill-md.test.ts`, `mcp-resume-run-tool.test.ts`: agree, and can fail. Each pinned phrase is absent from both sources on `main`. The new case sits in the tool's existing harness file and reads both tools off a real `tools/list`.

**The budget.** Counted in the gate's convention (bytes less the stamp line, over 4, rounded up): on `main` 23123 bytes, 422 lines, 5776 tokens; on this head 23270 bytes, 421 lines, 5813 tokens. The row grows by 251 bytes on its one line. The pitfall loses 104 bytes: a clause is deleted ("no execution path read it, so it produced no pause; `ToolSchema` is strict, so authoring it now fails the parse") and the two lines left are that deletion's own reflow. A real deletion, not a re-wrap; no re-wrap is counted as room. It pays the line count (minus one) and about 26 of the 63 added tokens. The other 37 come out of the file's existing headroom: the ceiling is 6801, no ceilings row is in the diff, and the gate's check-run is green. No ceiling moves, so no ruling is owed. See finding 3 for the wording.

**The deleted restatement has a home.** `## Tool metadata`, some forty lines up, keeps the rule: "`ToolSchema` is **strict** — an unknown key (a typo, or a retired one) is a parse error", and `requiresConfirmation` is named among the retired keys, "each rejection carries its replacement". The rationale that went ("no execution path read it") is in the rejection an author who writes the key is shown (`TOOL_RETIRED_KEY_GUIDANCE.requiresConfirmation`). The pitfall keeps the removal, its ADR and a pointer ("retired above") that resolves. No rule is lost.

**Tried to break it.**

- A delegated agent reading the account sentence: "for no person" excludes it, and its retry still works.
- An agent on a person's API key that takes itself for "an agent acting for itself": it hands off where `confirm: true` would have run. It errs toward not asserting an approval nobody gave.
- An account sending `confirm: true`, a truthy string or nothing, at MCP, REST or a host door under either posture: one refusal.
- Another gate answering first: the confirmation gate is last, so an account's malformed params get their `400` and a missing capability its `403` before any `428`. "Refused ... nothing runs" holds; the account sentence in the skill row promises no code.
- Resume with several candidate actions: the first that passes admits, so an account's run whose flow an ungated action also targets resumes. Each text ties the refusal to the gated action, so each holds.
- The agent as its own author: "its author declares `false`" could read as the agent's own move. An account's key is served the data skill with no authoring section; an OAuth caller's metadata edits land as drafts a person publishes. A person decides either way.
- stdio: it serves no action tools, as the row already says.
- The listing: see finding 2.

**Findings.**

1. **nit.** `mcp-http-tools.ts`, `resume_run` description: "the run stays paused: hand it to a person". The nearest noun is the run. The same description says only the user whose call started the run can resume it (the door answers anyone else its one not-found), and ADR-0151 D3 rule 3 names the door that hands a run to a person as not yet built. Every other carrier says "hand the action to a person". The reader's next step is the same under either reading (stop retrying, tell a person). Say "the action" when the file is next touched.
2. **nit.** All three client-facing texts hang the rule on what `list_actions` reports. The listing answers `actionLooksDestructive` (the declared flag, else `mode: 'delete'` or `variant: 'danger'`); the gate reads a declared `true` alone. An account therefore reads "refused whatever it sends" for an undeclared destructive-looking action that would run for it. The over-read is older than this diff (the person's sentence has it, harmlessly: always confirming is always correct) and for an account it errs to the safe side. The sentence's own subject, an action its author gated, is the declared flag, so the rule as written is true. A per-row `unavailable` computed from the declared flag is what settles it: carry this into the follow-up card.
3. **nit** (prose faces). The PR body and the skills changeset say the growth is "funded by" the pitfall trim. Measured, the trim funds the line count and under half the tokens; plus 37 is taken from headroom, as the body's own next sentence says. The card's acceptance names `check:skill-line-ratchet`, which does not price `skills/**`; the token ratchet does, and it is green under an unmoved ceiling. Accepted as it stands.
4. **nit** (lane seat's remainder). The dogfood header's stale sentence, ③.

Four nits; no should-fix, no must-fix. No delta review is owed.

**VERDICT: PASS**
